{{orphan|date=May 2017}}'''Orthogonal Signal Correction (OSC)''' is a spectral preprocessing technique that removes variation from a data matrix X that is [[Orthogonality|orthogonal]] to the response matrix Y.<ref>{{Citation
  | last1 = Wold
  | first1 = Svante
  | last2 = Antti
  | first2 = Henrik
  | last3 = Lindgren
  | first3 = F
  | last4 = Ohman
  | first4 = J
  | title = Orthogonal signal correction of near-infrared spectra
  | journal = Chemometrics and Intelligent Laboratory Systems
  | volume = 44
  | pages = 175–185
  | year = 1998
  | issue = 1–2
 | doi = 10.1016/s0169-7439(98)00109-9
  }}
</ref> OSC was introduced by researchers at the [[University of Umea]] in 1998 and has since found  applications in domains including [[metabolomics]].<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Mao H, Wang H, Wang B, etal|title=Systemic metabolic changes of traumatic critically ill patients revealed by an NMR-based metabonomic approach |journal=J. Proteome Res. |volume=8 |issue=12 |pages=5423–30 |year=2009|pmid=19835422 |doi=10.1021/pr900576y }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Tzovaras VT, Psychogios NG, Kostara CE, Bairaktari ET, Elisaf MS |title=Evaluation of the proximal tubular function in individuals with primary renal hypouricemia: an NMR-based metabonomic study |journal=NMR Biomed |volume=22 |issue=10 |pages=1072–83 |year=2009|pmid=19593759 |doi=10.1002/nbm.1415 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Gu H, Pan Z, Xi B, etal|title=1H NMR metabolomics study of age profiling in children |journal=NMR Biomed |volume=22 |issue=8 |pages=826–33 |year=2009 |pmid=19441074 |doi=10.1002/nbm.1395 |pmc=4009993}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Brindle JT, Nicholson JK, Schofield PM, Grainger DJ, Holmes E |title=Application of chemometrics to 1H NMR spectroscopic data to investigate a relationship between human serum metabolic profiles and hypertension |journal=Analyst |volume=128 |issue=1 |pages=32–6 |year=2003 |pmid=12572799 |doi= 10.1039/b209155k|bibcode=2003Ana...128...32B }}</ref>
